effect: An AI government no longer pays off every protest movement that has a budget demand. When a movement demanded more spending or a tax change, the AI moved that line half of the remaining way to the demand every 30 days until 98% met, whatever the movement's strength, so a weak movement got the same as a mass one; cost was checked only by the budget's own guard. Now the concession depends on the movement's strength, the larger of its mobilisation and its threat to the regime (both 0 to 1): below 0.45 there is no budget concession; above it the step is half the gap x strength / 0.7 (full half-step at 0.7 and above), halved again when the government's fiscal room is below 0.2. Union deals, public-wage offers, peace, civil-liberty and law concessions and the order posture are unchanged. Real-world behaviour: governments concede in proportion to the threat a movement poses and to what they can afford, and wait out weak protests (from memory). Day-0 effect: none (no movement exists at the start; the first opens around day 49 on seed 12345). By day 200, 20 movements carried a budget demand and 7 of them were strong enough to win concessions. No new saved state.
